_clamp() remains as defence-in-depth for direct/programmatic calls (server.py:105-106,157,221).
gaps: Tools use function-parameter schemas without an explicit pydantic model_config strict=True / extra='forbid'; type coercion is left at FastMCP defaults and extra fields are not provably forbidden by additionalProperties:false.

evidence: The server holds at most one of the three trifecta legs: no private-data access (public catalogue metadata only), no external send/write capability. Confirmed by grep — no smtplib/send_mail/.post()/webhook/slack anywhere in src.
All 13 tools are annotated readOnlyHint:true, destructiveHint:false (server.py:77) and only issue GET requests to one trusted host.
Posture is documented: SECURITY.md states 'no write, send, or filesystem capabilities, and no personal data is processed'; README describes Phase 1 read-only-first architecture (README.md:100-134).
Egress destination is a frozenset, not runtime-mutable (client.py:28), so no send-side allow-list can be widened at runtime.
gaps: The read-only/no-send assessment is documented in SECURITY.md/README prose rather than as an explicitly labelled 'Lethal Trifecta' scoring table.

evidence: grep for os.system(, shell=True, eval(, exec(, os.popen(, subprocess across src/ returns nothing — the server is a pure httpx API client.
No subprocess/shell usage anywhere in the Python code base (repo-wide grep, excluding .git).
No user input is ever passed to a shell; upstream calls go through httpx with URL-encoded params (client.py fetch_json).
Code-layer allow-list is a frozenset, not env-configurable: ALLOWED_HOSTS = frozenset({'api.i14y.admin.ch'}) (client.py:28).

assert_host_allowed() is called before the client is built (client.py:79) and follow_redirects=False refuses off-host 3xx (client.py:86,152-156); every request uses the fixed BASE_URL client so no request escapes the allow-list.
Tested: test_egress_allow_list_rejects_foreign_host, test_build_client_does_not_follow_redirects, test_redirect_is_refused (test_client.py).

docs/network-egress.md documents allow-listed hosts, both layers, the network-layer NetworkPolicy/firewall guidance including DNS on 53, and the reviewed update procedure; CHANGELOG references SEC-021.
gaps: The network-layer egress control is provided as documented per-deployment guidance (K8s NetworkPolicy / cloud firewall in docs/network-egress.md) rather than a committed enforced manifest, since the repo ships no fixed cloud deployment (compose has no native egress filtering).

evidence: Hash-pinning is implemented and enforced: tool_manifest() produces a deterministic sha256 over tool name + argument names + required set, committed to tool-definitions.lock.json (13 tools) and checked in CI by test_tool_manifest_matches_committed_lock (server.py:625-666; tests/test_tools.py).
CHANGELOG documents the lock and the rug-pull guard rationale (CHANGELOG SEC-022 entry); SECURITY.md describes it as the rug-pull control.
Tool definitions are static/in-repo with no dynamic or remote registration.
gaps: Tool names have NO server-identity namespace prefix (e.g. get_dataset, search_catalog instead of i14y__get_dataset), so cross-server tool shadowing behind a shared gateway is not structurally prevented — the first pass-criterion is unmet.
The lock hash deliberately excludes tool descriptions (only name + argument surface), so a description-only rug-pull would not be detected by the hash and relies on PR review instead.
